title: Continuous lattice coefficient sheaves and the integral inclusion
statement: For a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme], use its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For a commutative topological ring $T$, let $T_X$ be the sheaf of commutative rings with sections $T_X(U)=C(|U|,T)$, the continuous functions with pointwise operations, and restrictions given by precomposition with the underlying continuous maps of site morphisms. In the universe encoding for $X:\mathrm{Scheme}_{u}$ and $T:\mathrm{Type}_{u}$ the section type is $\mathrm{ULift}_{u+1}C(|U|,T)$. Write $T_X^{\mathrm{ring}}$ for the same sheaf after forgetting commutativity. Now let $\ell$ be prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension with canonical absolute value and valuation ring [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Equip $E$ with that absolute-value topology, represented by $\mathrm{WithAbs}(|\cdot|_E)$, and let $A=\{x\in E:|x|_E\leq1\}$ have its subspace topology. The integral coefficient map $a_X:A_X\to E_X$ is postcomposition with the actual inclusion $A\hookrightarrow E$ on every site object.
